findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

Removing `ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the hostname check means any caller-supplied `url` is fetched directly via `urllib.request.urlopen`. A malicious or compromised customer endpoint value such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (cloud instance metadata), `http://127.0.0.1:<internal-port>/`, or an RFC1918 admin service will be requested from the server with the event payload as the body.

Restore an egress policy before merge: keep a deny-by-default host allowlist (or per-tenant registered callback URLs), require `https`, resolve DNS and reject private/link-local/metadata literal IPs (including after redirect), and do not follow redirects to blocked ranges. Product support for customer endpoints must be layered on that policy — deleting the guard is not sufficient.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change opens unrestricted server-side request forgery (SSRF) on the webhook delivery path.

## Narrative

`deliver()` previously refused any host outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS`. This PR deletes that allowlist and posts the event to whatever `url` the caller supplies. On a runner or app server that can reach link-local metadata, localhost, or RFC1918 services, a customer-controlled (or attacker-influenced) endpoint can make the process fetch internal resources and return status (and potentially response-driven side effects) from those targets.

Supporting customer-owned webhook URLs is a valid product goal, but it needs an egress policy — HTTPS-only, DNS rebinding-safe resolution, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, and ideally an allowlist or per-tenant registered endpoint — not a raw `urlopen` on the supplied string.

No other files in the repo add compensating controls; this is the entire delivery surface.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
